axe: A tool for felling trees or chopping wood etc.
axed: simple past and past participle of ax (all etymologies and senses)
axel: A jump that includes one (or more than one) complete turn and a half turn while in the air.
axeman: A man who wields an axe.
axenic: Containing only a single species of microorganism.
axial: Relating to, resembling, or situated on an axis
axially: In relation to, or in a line with, an axis; in the axial (magnetic) line.
axil: The angle or point of divergence between the upper side of a branch, leaf, or petiole, and the stem or branch from which it springs.
axile: Situated in the axis of anything; as an embryo which lies in the axis of a seed.
axilla: The armpit, or the cavity beneath the junction of the arm and shoulder.
axillary: Of or pertaining to the axilla or armpit.
axing: present participle and gerund of ax
axiological: Of or relating to value theory, the philosophical field of axiology.
axiology: The study of value(s), as regards origin, nature, functions, types, and interrelations; value theory.
axiom: A seemingly self-evident or necessary truth which is based on assumption; a principle or proposition which cannot actually be proved or disproved.
axiomatically: By the use of axioms; in the form of an axiom.
axiomatization: The reduction of some system or concept to a set of axioms.
axiomatize: To establish a set of axioms that describe or govern certain phenomena
axiomatized: simple past and past participle of axiomatize
axiomatizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of axiomatize
axiomatizing: present participle and gerund of axiomatize
axion: A hypothetical subatomic particle postulated to resolve certain symmetry problems concerning the strong nuclear force.
axis: An imaginary line around which an object spins (an axis of rotation) or is symmetrically arranged (an axis of symmetry).
axised: Having the specified number or kind of axes.
axises: Misspelling of axes; mistakenly used for the plural of axis (“line around which object rotates”).
axisymmetric: Exhibiting symmetry around an axis; exhibiting cylindrical symmetry; axially symmetric
axisymmetry: symmetry about an axis; rotational symmetry
axled: Having (a specified number or kind of) axles.
axletree: A bar or beam of wood or iron, connecting the opposite wheels of a carriage, on the ends of which the wheels revolve.
axlike: Resembling or characteristic of an ax.
axolotl: A critically endangered salamander found in the elevated lakes of Mexico, Ambystoma mexicanum.
axon: A nerve fibre which is a long slender projection of a nerve cell, and which conducts nerve impulses away from the body of the cell to a synapse.
axonal: Of or pertaining to an axon.
axonemal: Of or pertaining to an axoneme
axoneme: A bundle of nine microtubules forming the internal scaffolding of a cilium, with two extra central microtubules connecting the others if the cilium is motile
axonometric: Describing a projection in which the horizontal and vertical axes are to the same scale, but the third axis is reduced to allow for perspective.
